text:
Filip Forsberg has 20 points in 17 games, and the surprise is how he's getting them: 15 assists and only 5 goals. In his last ten games he has nine helpers, and Roman Josi was asked about his passing after the 4-1 win over Carolina, the night Shane Wright made his Nashville debut alongside him.

Our numbers say to enjoy it but not to bank it. The Predators have scored 7.9 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. His own shooting is the opposite story: 5 goals on 5.9 expected and an 11.6% shooting rate, below his usual range. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him better than his goals, too.

So expect the mix to flip. The assists should slow and the goals should come. Our season-end range runs 71 to 98 points with 33 goals in the middle, which would still be a strong year at 32.
headline: Forsberg is passing more, and getting bounces
